documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine 6-month DM/HTN.

No new problems. Home BP 120s-130s/70s-80s. Taking meds daily. Never did the FIT.

Exam: well. Weight stable. Heart regular, S4. Lungs clear. Ext no edema.

A1c 7.5. Same plan - metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, amlodipine 10, ASA. BMP today. RTC Sept AWV.

documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Diabetic retinal exam, date of service 06/11/2024. Patient Carl Clark.
VA 20/25 OU cc. Dilated: no retinopathy, no edema OU.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV

Says he's fine. Hot summer, not as hungry, "lost a couple pounds without trying, which is fine by me." Still walking, maybe a bit less. No falls. Independent.
PHQ-2 0.

Meds unchanged.

Exam: weight down about 2 kg from March. BP good. Heart regular, S4. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Feet normal.

A/P:
- Wellness: as above. Will watch the weight at next visit.
- T2DM: A1c and urine microalbumin today. Lipid panel.
- Colonoscopy: offered again; declines.
- Flu + COVID 10/8.

RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Clark - A1c is down to 7.1, which is good, though I suspect part of it is that you've been eating less. Urine protein normal, cholesterol similar to prior years. We'll check your weight again at the next visit.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, losing weight.

HPI: 72M seen after RN flagged fatigue at his flu shot. Says since about July he has been more and more tired and has lost weight without trying - about 10 lb by his bathroom scale. Fills up after half a plate. The last few weeks a mild ache under the right ribs, comes and goes, not related to meals that he can tell. Bowels irregular, constipated some days, normal others. No nausea or vomiting. No black or bloody stools that he has seen. No fever, sweats, cough. No jaundice noticed by wife.

Meds unchanged. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol. Father - colon cancer at 70. Has never had a colonoscopy.

Exam: Looks thinner than in the spring. Weight about 70 kg (about 74 most of the last several years). BP and HR fine. Afebrile. Sclerae anicteric. No lymphadenopathy in neck or supraclavicular areas. Heart regular, S4. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft; the liver edge is firm and palpable below the right costal margin, not particularly tender. No ascites appreciable. No edema.

A/P:
1. Unintentional weight loss, early satiety, RUQ discomfort, palpable liver, constipation, in a man with a strong family history and no colon screening. Concerned about a malignancy, including colorectal. CMP and CBC today. Urgent GI referral placed - called the GI office myself and they will see him 11/12.
2. Fatigue - as above.
3. DM/HTN - BP lower with the weight loss; continue for now.

We talked openly about why I am worried. He and his wife (on speaker) understand. I'll call with labs.

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt with results. Liver tests are abnormal: AST/ALT mildly up, alk phos clearly elevated, bilirubin borderline, albumin low-normal. Hgb 13.2, a little lower than his usual. Kidney function fine.

These fit with something going on in the liver and support seeing GI quickly. Confirmed 11/12 appointment; GI has the labs. He asked whether he should stop metformin - no, continue for now. Wife on the line, questions answered.

events.reason: Weight loss, early satiety, abnormal liver tests

reports.text:
Technique: CT of the abdomen after IV contrast, portal venous phase.
Liver: multiple hypoattenuating lesions in both lobes, the largest 4.6 cm in the right lobe. No biliary ductal dilation.
Gallbladder: unremarkable.
Pancreas, spleen, adrenals: unremarkable.
Kidneys: enhance symmetrically, no hydronephrosis.
Bowel: irregular mass-like wall thickening of the ascending colon. No bowel obstruction.
No ascites. No free air.
Vessels: normal caliber abdominal aorta.
Bones: no destructive lesion.
reports.conclusion:
1. Irregular mass-like wall thickening of the ascending colon, suspicious for primary colon neoplasm.
2. Multiple hypoattenuating liver lesions in both lobes, largest 4.6 cm, suspicious for metastases.
3. No biliary dilation, ascites or obstruction.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 11/12/2024
Patient: Carl Clark   DOB: 09/28/1952
Referring: primary care (urgent)

Reason: fatigue, weight loss, abnormal liver tests.

History: 72-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidemia, seen by cardiology in 2019, who describes four months of steadily worsening fatigue with unplanned weight loss. He gets full quickly, has a mild discomfort in the right upper quadrant and his bowels have become intermittently constipated. He has not had nausea or vomiting and has not seen blood in the stool. He has never had hepatitis or any liver disease that he knows of. He has never had a colonoscopy or any other cancer screening. He does not smoke or drink and takes nothing hepatotoxic.

Medications (per patient list): metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father with colon cancer at 70, deceased. Mother with diabetes and hypertension.

Examination: Thin man, comfortable. No scleral icterus. Abdomen soft. A firm liver edge is felt 3 cm below the right costal margin; it is not tender. No ascites by exam.

Labs today: AST 51, ALT 44, alkaline phosphatase 189, total bilirubin 1.4, albumin 3.4, INR 1.1. AFP within normal limits.

CT abdomen with IV contrast (done today): multiple liver lesions in both lobes, the largest 4.6 cm, and irregular thickening of the ascending colon wall. Report attached.

Impression: Colorectal neoplasia, likely arising in the ascending colon, with liver lesions that are highly suspicious for metastatic disease.

Plan:
1. Colonoscopy with biopsy - booked 11/21.
2. Image-guided core biopsy of a representative liver lesion through interventional radiology.
3. Oncology referral once tissue is in hand.
4. I discussed these findings frankly with Mr. Clark and his wife.

Thank you for this referral.
Gastroenterology

events.reason: Colonoscopy for colon mass on CT

reports.text:
Specimen: ascending colon mass, biopsies (5 fragments).
Gross: tan-pink soft tissue fragments, 0.2 to 0.5 cm, submitted entirely.
Microscopic: fragments of colonic mucosa infiltrated by malignant glands with cribriform architecture, nuclear stratification and dirty necrosis, invading into submucosa present in the sample.
reports.conclusion: Ascending colon mass, biopsy: invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOSCOPY CENTER - COLONOSCOPY REPORT
Date: 11/21/2024. Patient: Carl Clark, 72 M.
Indication: colonic wall thickening and liver lesions on CT; weight loss.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. ASA III.
Prep: good (BBPS 7).

Findings:
- Cecum reached, identified by appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve.
- Ascending colon: ulcerated, friable mass; the scope passed beyond it. Multiple cold forceps biopsies taken. Area tattooed distally.
- No other lesions to the cecum. Remainder of colon to rectum normal.
- Retroflexion in rectum: normal.

Impression: ascending colon mass, malignant in appearance.

Pathology (received 11/25): invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated.

Plan: liver lesion biopsy via IR, oncology referral. Results discussed with patient by phone.
Allergies: NKDA.

Gastroenterology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with his wife to talk through the GI findings.

Colonoscopy report and pathology received 12/2: ascending colon mass, biopsy invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated. CT 11/12 with multiple liver lesions in both lobes suspicious for spread. Liver biopsy by IR is scheduled 12/19. GI has referred him to oncology; first visit January 6.

He is quieter than usual but asking good questions. "I should have done the test." We talked about that honestly and about where things go from here. Appetite still small; eating a few small meals. Weight stable since October. RUQ ache unchanged, tolerable without medication. Bowels about the same. Sleeping OK. PHQ-2 1.

Exam: thin, NAD. Anicteric. Liver edge palpable as before. Heart regular. Lungs clear.

A/P:
1. Adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon with probable liver metastases - awaiting liver biopsy and oncology consult. Explained staging and what oncology will likely discuss. Will help coordinate.
2. T2DM - eating less; fasting sugars running 110s-130s at home. Continue metformin 1000 BID for now; call if readings under 80.
3. HTN - pressures lower with weight loss; continue for now, home log.
4. Support - offered social work and the cancer center's support programs; wife will look into the caregiver group.

Total time 45 minutes, majority counseling.

documents.title: biopsy done
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just letting you know they did the liver biopsy Thursday. A little sore, that's all. They said the oncologist will go over the results January 6. Merry Christmas to everyone there.

documents.title: RE: biopsy done
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update, Carl. Glad it went smoothly. I'll look for the oncology note after the 6th. Call us if the soreness gets worse or you have a fever. Merry Christmas to you and your wife.
